stories.headline: Iran's IRGC says mines set two more tankers ablaze near Hormuz, claims US MQ-9 downed

key_facts.fact: On Tuesday, October 20, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two oil tankers were set ablaze and halted after hitting IRGC naval mines at what Tehran calls an illegal crossing point in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: "Two violating oil tankers were set ablaze and halted due to the explosion of mines planted by the brave sailors of the IRGC Navy at an illegal crossing point in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz," the Guards said in a statement published on their official Sepah News website.

key_facts.fact: Iran International reported the IRGC Navy said the two tankers hit mines on Monday night (October 19), did not identify the vessels or report casualties, and warned that ships crossing the mined passage could be set ablaze.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's IRGC Navy said on Tuesday that two oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in a passage south of the Strait of Hormuz on Monday night, and were stopped... It warned that ships crossing the mined passage could be set ablaze, but did not identify the tankers or report any casualties.

key_facts.fact: The Guards also said they shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone; this came a day after the IRGC said another tanker caught fire after hitting a mine, and two days after it said two other tankers had hit mines.
key_facts.excerpt: The Revolutionary Guards also said they had shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone. On Monday, the Guards said a tanker caught fire after hitting a mine, while the day before it said two other tankers had hit mines.

key_facts.fact: US Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper said the strait is controlled by the US and regional partners and 'remains open for business,' citing about 400 merchant ship transits in the previous week.
key_facts.excerpt: CentCom chief Adm. Brad Cooper said in a video message the Strait of Hormuz "is controlled by the United States and our regional partners, not Iran, and it remains open for business." He added about 400 merchant ships transited the strait in the previous week

key_facts.fact: Reuters reported on October 20, citing three senior Iranian officials and an insider, that Iran is deliberately prolonging talks with Washington to weaken Trump before the November 3 midterm elections while preparing for renewed US and Israeli strikes.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has deliberately prolonged talks with the United States in an effort to weaken President Donald Trump politically before the November 3 midterm elections, Reuters reported on Tuesday, citing three senior Iranian officials and an Iranian insider. One unnamed Iranian official told Reuters: "Iran is preparing for renewed Israeli and US attacks, not for a deal with America to end the war."

key_facts.fact: Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, a key US-Iran mediator this year, arrived in Tehran on Tuesday to meet senior Iranian officials amid stalled talks.
key_facts.excerpt: Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Field Marshal Asim Munir arrived in Tehran on Tuesday to meet senior Iranian officials... Pakistan has played a key mediating role between the US and Iran this year.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude stood above $109.8 a barrel on Tuesday (Beijing midday) and WTI at $98.71, as Iran war risks offset hopes for more Russian supply.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent oil remains above $109.8 per barrel (slightly up 0.26%) as of Tuesday (12.50pm Beijing on Tuesday, October 20, 2026), as Iran war risks offset hopes for more Russian supply. WTI crude stood at $98.71 per barrel

stories.headline: UK sends RAF Typhoon jets to defend Saudi Arabia from escalating Houthi attacks

key_facts.fact: On October 20, the UK Ministry of Defence announced RAF Typhoon fighter jets will fly defensive counter-air missions to protect Saudi cities and critical national infrastructure from aerial attack, and will not conduct offensive strikes against the Houthis.
key_facts.excerpt: The UK will fly defensive counter air missions to support the protection of Saudi cities and critical national infrastructure against aerial attack, using RAF Typhoon fighter jets. These aircraft will operate in a defensive role and will not conduct offensive strikes against the Houthis.

key_facts.fact: The UK will also provide an RAF A400M transport aircraft, military advisers to Saudi staff officers, and an extension of air-to-air refuelling support for Saudi air operations, including those to degrade Houthi targets in Yemen.
key_facts.excerpt: The UK will provide an RAF A400M to support the movement of defence materiel within Saudi Arabia, alongside UK military advisers to support Saudi staff officers... It also includes an extension of air-to-air refuelling support for Saudi defensive air operations including to degrade Houthi military targets in Yemen

key_facts.fact: Defence Secretary Wes Streeting called the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia 'absolutely despicable', citing the targeting of Riyadh's airport.
key_facts.excerpt: The continuing attacks from the Houthis on our ally Saudi Arabia are absolutely despicable. The targeting of the airport in Riyadh in particular shows the lengths the Houthis are going to escalate the situation in the region.

key_facts.fact: The support follows a request from the Saudi government and expands a September package that included an RAF Voyager refuelling aircraft but no fighter jets.
key_facts.excerpt: The additional support follows a request from Saudi Arabia's government, which Prime Minister Andy Burnham said earlier this month Britain was prepared to consider. Britain will also deploy an Atlas A400M transport aircraft and military advisers, expanding assistance announced in September which included an RAF Voyager air-to-air refuelling aircraft but not fighter jets.

key_facts.fact: Houthi strikes on Riyadh's airport have killed more than a dozen people in October, and Yemeni authorities said on Monday a Houthi strike on a government security forces training camp killed 58 people.
key_facts.excerpt: Houthi attacks have intensified in Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, with Yemen authorities saying on Monday that a strike on a government security forces training camp had killed 58 people. Strikes on Riyadh's airport have killed more than a dozen people and disrupted flights in October

stories.headline: Japan launches MMX, first mission aiming to bring back samples from Mars' moon Phobos

key_facts.fact: JAXA's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) spacecraft launched on October 19 at 3:41 p.m. EDT (19:41 GMT) on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima Space Center, the 10th H3 flight.
key_facts.excerpt: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launched today (Oct. 19) from Tanegashima Space Center in Japan, riding an H3 rocket that lifted off ... at 3:41 p.m. EDT (1941 GMT; 4:41 a.m. local time in Japan on Oct. 20). It was the 10th liftoff of Japan's expendable, two-stage H3 rocket

key_facts.fact: JAXA confirmed the probe separated from the rocket over an hour after liftoff and was 'beginning its journey towards the Martian system'; arrival near Mars is expected around August 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Over an hour later, JAXA announced during the livestream that the probe had successfully separated from the H3 and was "beginning its journey towards the Martian system". The spacecraft is due to arrive near Mars around August next year

key_facts.fact: MMX plans two touchdowns on Phobos to collect at least 10 grams of soil, with the sample capsule due to land in Australia in 2031; it would be the first sample return from a Martian moon.
key_facts.excerpt: MMX will perform two separate touchdowns on Phobos to collect and stow samples in the spacecraft's return capsule... If all goes according to plan, the MMX sample-return capsule will land in Australia in 2031.

key_facts.fact: The spacecraft carries the German-French Idefix rover (DLR and CNES), set to land on Phobos around the turn of 2028/2029 and become the first rover to drive on a Martian moon, exploring for about 100 days.
key_facts.excerpt: The Idefix rover, developed jointly by DLR and CNES, is scheduled to land on Mars' moon Phobos around the turn of the year 2028/2029 and explore it for approximately 100 days.

key_facts.fact: NASA has invested about $87 million through the end of the mission and will receive at least 15% of the planned 10-gram Phobos sample; it contributed the MEGANE spectrometer and a Honeybee Robotics pneumatic sampler.
key_facts.excerpt: NASA has also invested approximately $87 million through the end of the mission... At least 15% of the planned 10-gram (0.35 ounces) returned Phobos sample will be reserved for NASA's study.

key_facts.fact: China's Tianwen-3 is scheduled to launch around 2028 and aims to return Mars samples as early as 2031, potentially before the Japanese mission.
key_facts.excerpt: China's Tianwen-3 spacecraft is scheduled for launch around 2028 and aims to return Mars samples to Earth as early as 2031 — potentially before the Japanese mission's return.

stories.headline: FDA approves GSK's Jemperli as first immunotherapy for some locally advanced rectal cancers

key_facts.fact: On October 19, the FDA granted accelerated approval to GSK's Jemperli (dostarlimab) alone for adults with previously untreated stage II or III locally advanced rectal cancer whose tumors are mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) or microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H).
key_facts.excerpt: Today's approval is for Jemperli used alone in adults with previously untreated stage II or stage III locally advanced rectal cancer... patients' tumors must be mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) or microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H), as determined by an FDA-authorized test.

key_facts.fact: In the 154-patient phase 2 AZUR-1 trial, after median follow-up of more than two years almost three-fourths of patients had not needed surgery, radiotherapy or chemotherapy.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA based its decision on interim results from AZUR-1... in 154 patients... After a median follow-up of more than 2 years... almost three-fourths of patients had not needed surgery, radiotherapy or chemotherapy.

key_facts.fact: GSK said 68% of evaluable patients achieved a sustained clinical complete response at 12 months by investigator assessment (47% by independent central review, data still maturing), with no recurrences among responders to date.
key_facts.excerpt: Investigator-assessed data... showed 68% of evaluable patients (98/144...) achieved cCR12... 47% (54/116)... of evaluable patients have achieved cCR12... No disease recurrences have been reported among responders to date, after a median follow up of more than two years.

key_facts.fact: The MSI-H/dMMR biomarker is found in around 5-10% of rectal cancers; standard treatment of chemotherapy, radiation and surgery can cause lasting bowel, urinary and sexual dysfunction and infertility.
key_facts.excerpt: Current standard of treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer includes chemotherapy, radiation and surgery, but these can have lasting consequences, including bowel, urinary and sexual dysfunction, secondary cancers and infertility. For patients with MSI-H/dMMR tumors, a biomarker found in around 5-10% of rectal cancers

key_facts.fact: The review ran under the FDA Commissioner's National Priority Voucher pilot program and the approval came 4 months ahead of the FDA goal date.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA approved this application 4 months ahead of the FDA goal date. This application is part of the FDA Commissioner's National Priority Review Voucher (CNPV) pilot program

key_facts.fact: Serious adverse reactions occurred in 20% of patients and 3% discontinued treatment; GSK will present full AZUR-1 interim data at the ESMO Congress in October 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Serious adverse reactions occurred in 20% of patients receiving Jemperli... Jemperli was permanently discontinued due to adverse reactions in 3% of patients. Full data from the AZUR-1 interim analysis will be presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress in October 2026.

stories.headline: US sanctions China's MiraclePlus VC firm over ex-Google engineer's AI trade-secret theft

key_facts.fact: On October 19, the US State Department designated five China-based entities under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act (PAIPA): Shanghai Zhisuan Technology, venture firm MiraclePlus, and three MiraclePlus-linked funds and entities.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, the Department of State announced the designations of five entities under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act (PAIPA) in connection with theft of trade secrets from U.S. persons.

key_facts.fact: Zhisuan was founded in 2023 by former Google engineer Linwei Ding, who pitched MiraclePlus's incubator by claiming Zhisuan could replicate Google's AI infrastructure; MiraclePlus gave seed capital in exchange for a stake.
key_facts.excerpt: Ding applied on behalf of Zhisuan to a China-based startup incubation program known as MiraclePlus, touting his experience with and knowledge of Google's technology and internal systems and claiming that Zhisuan could replicate Google's SI infrastructure technology... MiraclePlus gave seed capital in exchange for an ownership stake in Zhisuan.

key_facts.fact: Ding was convicted on January 29 of seven counts of economic espionage and seven counts of theft of trade secrets; he was sentenced to a year in jail in September.
key_facts.excerpt: Ding, also known as Leon Ding, was convicted on Jan. 29 of seven counts of economic espionage and seven counts of theft of trade secrets, according to a DOJ press release.

key_facts.fact: Sanctions include property blocking, banking and foreign-exchange restrictions, a cap on US loans above $10 million in 12 months, and a ban on US persons buying significant equity or debt; OFAC allowed wind-down of MiraclePlus dealings until January 19, 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: the PAIPA sanctions apply to all five entities include property blocking and transaction prohibitions... restrictions on foreign-exchange and banking transactions... a prohibition on U.S. financial institutions providing loans or credit totaling more than $10 million in any 12-month period... General License 2 authorizes transactions ordinarily incident and necessary to wind down dealings involving MiraclePlus... through 12:01 a.m. ET on Jan. 19.

key_facts.fact: MiraclePlus was founded by former Microsoft and Baidu AI executive Lu Qi as the successor to Y Combinator's abandoned China program, and has backed SiliconFlow and robotics maker AgiBot, both considering Hong Kong listings.
key_facts.excerpt: Lu's MiraclePlus, the successor to a Chinese program run by Silicon Valley's Y Combinator, and three affiliates drew sanctions for providing seed financing to Zhisuan... It's since backed some of China's most promising startups, including AI inference platform SiliconFlow and robotics maker AgiBot, both of which are considering Hong Kong listings.

stories.headline: GCash parent Mynt debuts in Manila after the Philippines' largest-ever IPO

key_facts.fact: Mynt Inc., operator of the GCash mobile wallet, listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange on October 20 under ticker GCASH after raising 60.9 billion pesos, the largest IPO in the exchange's history; President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. led the bell-ringing.
key_facts.excerpt: The bell ringing ceremony to mark its official listing on October 20, 2026, was spearheaded by President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. Trading under the ticker symbol GCASH, the company raised an astounding Php 60.9 billion

key_facts.fact: Mynt sold about 8.03 billion shares at 6.60 pesos each; the overallotment raised the deal from about 53 billion pesos to 60.9 billion pesos (about $967 million), surpassing Monde Nissin's 55.89 billion-peso IPO in 2021.
key_facts.excerpt: The offering surpassed Monde Nissin Corp.'s P55.89-billion IPO in 2021... Mynt sold approximately 8.03 billion common shares at P6.60 apiece... the exercise of an overallotment option covering about 1.20 billion additional secondary shares increased the total transaction size to P60.9 billion.

key_facts.fact: Mynt debuted with a market capitalization of 441.5 billion pesos (about $7 billion), making it the seventh-largest domestic company on the PSE.
key_facts.excerpt: "Today, Mynt debuts with a market capitalization of P441.5 billion, or about $7 billion," said Monzon. The PSE chief said Mynt is the seventh largest domestic company in the PSE

key_facts.fact: Shares rose as much as 1.7% to 6.71 pesos intraday amid a broader Asian sell-off in AI-related shares, but closed at the IPO price.
key_facts.excerpt: Shares of fintech firm Mynt, operator of mobile wallet GCash, rose 1.7 per cent in its market debut on Tuesday (Oct 20)... The stock opened at 6.60 pesos a share, in line with its offer price, before rising to 6.71 pesos... even as a broader sell-off in AI-related shares made investors more selective about new tech listings.

key_facts.fact: GMA News reported Mynt closed its first trading day at the IPO price.
key_facts.excerpt: GCash parent Mynt closes at IPO price on market debut, raises P60.9 billion

key_facts.fact: More than 20 cornerstone investors including BlackRock, Citadel, Fidelity International and the IFC committed about $500 million, nearly 60% of the base deal.
key_facts.excerpt: The Mynt IPO attracted more than 20 cornerstone investors, who committed about US$500 million, or nearly 60 per cent of the base deal... Investors included BlackRock, Citadel, Fidelity International and the International Finance Corp.

key_facts.fact: BusinessWorld reported Mynt plans to allocate 60% of net primary proceeds to its CreditTech business, with the rest for product development and general corporate purposes.
key_facts.excerpt: Based on its final IPO prospectus, Mynt plans to allocate 60% of the net proceeds from the primary offering to the expansion of its credit technology (CreditTech) business.

stories.headline: Chip stocks snap 8-day slide as 10-year Treasury yield climbs back to 5.14%

key_facts.fact: On Monday, October 19, the Nasdaq rose 1.11% to 26,430.89 and the S&P 500 gained 0.41% to 7,690.73, while the Dow slipped 0.07% to 51,966.03.
key_facts.excerpt: The tech-heavy index added 1.11% to end at 26,430.89 while the S&P 500 gained 0.41% to close at 7,690.73. The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished the day at 51,966.03, slipping 36.38 points, or 0.07%.

key_facts.fact: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 1.61%, ending an eight-session losing streak in which it fell 15.7%, its longest since October 2008; CoreWeave fell another 0.44% after dropping more than 25% the prior week over its roughly $50 billion debt load.
key_facts.excerpt: The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had fallen 15.7 percent over the previous eight sessions — its longest consecutive losing streak since October 2008 — before rising 1.61 percent Monday to snap the run... CoreWeave... fell another 0.44 percent. The company's share price had dropped more than 25 percent last week amid concerns about its roughly $50 billion debt load.

key_facts.fact: The 10-year Treasury yield rose 3.8 basis points to 5.135% on Monday, up 1.148 percentage points from a year earlier and 0.175 point below its 52-week high of 5.31% on October 5.
key_facts.excerpt: The 10-year yield rose 0.038 percentage point to 5.135% today... Yield is off 0.175 percentage point from its 52-week high of 5.310% hit Monday, Oct. 5, 2026... Yield is up 1.148 percentage points from 52 weeks ago

key_facts.fact: WTI crude settled up 2.22% at $103.66 a barrel on Monday while Brent fell 0.28% to $109.55, with traders watching Persian Gulf ship attacks and Ukraine-Russia strikes on energy infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: WTI settled up 2.22% at $103.66 per barrel, while Brent fell 0.28% to $109.55 per barrel... Traders were also keeping a wary eye on oil markets with ship attacks in the Persian Gulf picking up and Ukraine and Russia trading attacks on energy infrastructure.

key_facts.fact: Early Tuesday, the S&P 500 slipped 0.1% and the Nasdaq fell 0.5% as AI stocks swung again, with Meta, Micron and Intel lower, while European indexes fell again.
key_facts.excerpt: The S&P 500 slipped 0.1% early Tuesday to give back some of its gain from Monday. The losses for AI stocks sent the Nasdaq composite down 0.5%... Meta Platforms, Micron and Intel all fell... Stock indexes fell in Europe again.
